story: Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program, with a $272.7 million Year 2 award from CMS on November 9th, second only to Texas, and what the roughly $249 million Year 1 portfolio bought, including where AI shows up in it

claims.claim: CMS announced $10 billion in second-year Rural Health Transformation Program awards to all 50 states on November 9th.
claims.verbatim: $10 billion in awards to all 50 states for the second year of the Rural Health Transformation Program
claims.notes: Opening paragraph of the release. The release is dated Nov 09, 2026 and headlined 'Trump Administration Announces $10 Billion in Second Year of Rural Health Transformation Awards to All 50 States'. Inside the window.

claims.claim: Alaska's fiscal year 2027 Rural Health Transformation award is $272,653,149.
claims.notes: From the Alaska row of the FY 2027 award table, confirmed on two separate fetches. Compared with the Year 1 award of $272,174,855.72 (C30), Year 2 is about $478,000 higher. That difference is derived, so label it as derived if used. This release names Alaska only in the table, and it doesn't mention AI.

claims.claim: Texas received the largest Year 2 award, $281,976,026.
claims.notes: From the Texas row of the award table. A targeted fetch confirmed Texas as the single largest award. Stateline separately reports 'almost $282 million' for Texas, which is consistent, but that article couldn't be fetched (see killed).

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 2 award is the second largest of the 50 states, behind only Texas.
claims.notes: This ranking is my reading of the table, because the release itself never says 'second'. The fetched top six in order are Texas $281,976,026, Alaska $272,653,149, Montana $239,740,669, California $231,105,823, Oklahoma $227,097,543 and Kansas $225,896,117. In Year 1 Alaska was also second overall, according to the Alaska DOH (C29).

claims.claim: Montana's Year 2 award is $239,740,669, the third largest.
claims.notes: Montana row of the award table. The rank comes from the fetched top-six ordering.

claims.claim: California's Year 2 award is $231,105,823.
claims.notes: California row of the award table. It ranks fourth in the fetched ordering.

claims.claim: Oklahoma's Year 2 award is $227,097,543.
claims.notes: Oklahoma row of the award table. It ranks fifth in the fetched ordering, and Kansas is sixth at $225,896,117.

claims.claim: New Jersey received the smallest Year 2 award, $142,338,224.
claims.notes: New Jersey row. A targeted fetch confirmed it as the single smallest. The next smallest are Connecticut at $153,652,078 and Rhode Island at $158,171,967. Alaska's award is about 1.9 times New Jersey's, which is derived.

claims.claim: With the second-year awards, the federal government has now awarded $20 billion through the Rural Health Transformation Program.
claims.verbatim: the Trump Administration has now awarded $20 billion through the RHTP
claims.notes: Consistent with two $10 billion years out of a $50 billion five-year program (C31).

claims.claim: CMS says another $30 billion will be awarded over the program's remaining three years.
claims.verbatim: Over the remaining three years of the program, an additional $30 billion will be awarded
claims.notes: This is a forward commitment, not money already paid. Suggested wording is 'CMS expects to award another $30 billion' or 'is slated to award'. The arithmetic is consistent with C09 and C31 ($20B + $30B = $50B).

claims.claim: All 50 states submitted annual progress reports, which CMS reviewed in determining each state's Year 2 award.
claims.verbatim: All 50 states submitted annual reports documenting their progress, which CMS reviewed
claims.notes: The sentence ends 'as part of determining each state's award.' I confirmed it in two fragments on a targeted fetch.

claims.claim: CMS said Year 2 awards rested partly on state progress with rural health policies such as the Presidential Fitness Test and physician continuing education on nutrition.
claims.verbatim: such as the Presidential Fitness Test and Continuing Medical Education (CME) for physicians on nutrition
claims.notes: The page's wording just before 'such as' is 'state progress on implementation of state policies to improve rural health,'. The brief's paraphrase 'progress implementing state policies' doesn't match the page, so quote the page wording.

claims.claim: CMS said Year 2 awards also reflect, in part, each state's progress implementing its approved transformation plan.
claims.verbatim: This year's awards also reflect, in part, states' progress implementing their approved RHTP plans.
claims.notes: The apostrophe style on the live page may be curly, and the fetch rendered them straight.

claims.claim: Each state receives $100 million a year in baseline Rural Health Transformation funding.
claims.verbatim: each state receives $100 million in baseline funding each year
claims.notes: The fact sheet describes baseline as half of annual funding, split evenly among states. That checks out arithmetically, since $100M x 50 = $5B, which is half of $10B. So Alaska's Year 2 award is about $100M baseline plus about $172.7M workload funding (derived).

claims.claim: The other half of annual funding, called workload funding, weighs factors including the characteristics of a state's rural population and health facilities, its plan initiatives and certain state policy actions.
claims.verbatim: Characteristics of a state's rural population and healthcare facilities;
claims.notes: The other bullets in the list read 'Initiatives included in the state's rural health transformation plan;', 'Certain state policy actions;' and 'Other technical, data-driven factors described in the NOFO.'

claims.claim: Because workload funding is recalculated each year, CMS says a state's total award may rise, fall or stay similar from year to year.
claims.verbatim: a state's total award may increase, decrease, or remain similar from one year to the next.
claims.notes: Use this to keep the deck from implying that Alaska's roughly $272M is locked in for future years.

claims.claim: For Year 2, CMS weighed each state's initiative progress at checkpoints such as program governance, project plan approval, launching initiatives, reaching milestones, establishing methods for measuring results and planning for sustainability.
claims.verbatim: establishing program governance, developing and receiving approval of project plans, launching initiatives, reaching milestones, establishing methods for measuring results, and planning for long-term sustainability
claims.notes: The list continues 'reaching milestones, establishing methods for measuring results, and planning for long-term sustainability.' The fact sheet calls these examples. 'Six checkpoints' is my count of the examples, not CMS's number, so don't present six as an official total.

claims.claim: Tech innovation is one of the program's five strategic goals.
claims.verbatim: Tech innovation
claims.notes: The five goals as listed are 'Make rural America healthy again', 'Sustainable access', 'Workforce development', 'Innovative care' and 'Tech innovation'.

claims.claim: Technology-enabled care and health IT is one of the approved uses of program funds, and states must use funds for at least three approved uses.
claims.verbatim: technology-enabled care and health IT
claims.notes: The 'at least three approved uses' point comes from the fetch summary of the same section. The verbatim string covers the approved use only.

claims.claim: KFF Health News reported on November 5th that CMS missed its October 31st deadline to tell states their Year 2 award amounts.
claims.verbatim: CMS missed its Oct. 31 deadline to tell states how much they’ll get next year
claims.notes: The verbatim is the photo caption, printed with a curly apostrophe. The body reads 'State leaders had expected to hear their 2027 award amount by Oct. 31'. Bylines are Sarah Jane Tribble, Arielle Zionts and Bram Sable-Smith. The fetch summary says the delay was announced in a mass email on October 30th. The article doesn't mention Alaska. Attribute it as 'according to KFF Health News'. The awards came nine days after the deadline (derived).

claims.claim: CMS announced on October 22nd nearly $249 million in Rural Health Transformation funding for 254 Alaska projects.
claims.verbatim: nearly $249 million in Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding for 254 projects
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, since it predates the October 30th window. It independently corroborates the Alaska DOH figures (C26, C27). This CMS release gives no $272M figure and no Hedberg quote, names no grantees and has no AI mention. It describes the TCC, Maniilaq and Norton Sound projects without naming them.

claims.claim: The Alaska Department of Health announced on October 22nd the completion of its Year 1 Rural Health Transformation funding cycle.
claims.verbatim: today announced the completion of the Year 1 funding cycle for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP)
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, since it predates the window. WebFetch returned binary, so the fact-checker read the saved PDF directly and confirmed every quoted string. The showrunner's extraction was by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py, and the fact-checker read the PDF independently.

claims.claim: The final Year 1 Notices of Intent to Award were issued on October 9th.
claims.verbatim: The final Notices of Intent to Award for the first funding cycle were issued on October 9, 2026.
claims.notes: Background. Consistent with the funding update's final round, Week 8 on October 9th (C42).

claims.claim: The rest of Alaska's Year 1 award, beyond the project subawards, supports administration, evaluation and oversight of the program.
claims.verbatim: The remaining award balance supports administration, evaluation and oversight of the RHTP program.
claims.notes: Derived, not stated: the $272,174,855.72 award minus the workbook's $248,976,547.51 gives about $23.2M, roughly 8.5 percent. If the deck uses that figure, label it as a derived estimate from preliminary amounts.

claims.claim: According to the Alaska Department of Health, Alaska's Year 1 award was the highest per-capita award in the nation.
claims.verbatim: the highest per-capita award in the nation and the second-highest overall award amount.
claims.notes: This is the state's own characterization, and the November 9th CMS release doesn't rank states per capita. Attribute it with 'according to the Alaska Department of Health'. It refers to Year 1. Don't extend it to Year 2 without computing it.

claims.claim: The Alaska Department of Health says it has awarded just under $249 million in Year 1 funding.
claims.verbatim: DOH has awarded just under $249 million to 254 projects in communities across Alaska.
claims.notes: Corroborated by CMS (C21) and the workbook total (C48, $248,976,547.51). The amounts are preliminary per C45.

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 1 funding went to 254 projects.
claims.verbatim: DOH has awarded just under $249 million to 254 projects in communities across Alaska.
claims.notes: Corroborated by CMS (C21), by the funding update cumulative of 254 (C44) and by the workbook (C47). The weekly project counts in the update sum to 254.

claims.claim: According to the state, CMS awarded Alaska more than $272 million for Year 1.
claims.verbatim: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) awarded Alaska more than $272 million for Year 1
claims.notes: The DOH HTML page corroborates it: 'Alaska's year one award was $272,174,855.72 to support targeted, system-level investments.'

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 1 award was the second highest overall award amount, according to the state.
claims.verbatim: the highest per-capita award in the nation and the second-highest overall award amount.
claims.notes: This is Year 1. It makes Year 2 (C04) a second straight year at number two. 'Second year running' is supportable only if attributed to the state for Year 1.

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 1 federal financial assistance award totaled $272,174,855.72, fully funded by CMS.
claims.verbatim: a financial assistance award totaling $272,174,855.72 with 100 percent funded by CMS/HHS.
claims.notes: Funding disclaimer at the foot of the release. Corroborated verbatim on https://health.alaska.gov/en/education/rural-health-transformation-program/ as 'Alaska's year one award was $272,174,855.72', with the overview rounding it to '$272,174,856'.

claims.claim: The Rural Health Transformation Program is a $50 billion, five-year national initiative authorized by Congress in 2025.
claims.verbatim: RHTP is part of a $50 billion, five-year national initiative authorized by Congress in 2025 to strengthen rural health systems.
claims.notes: KFF Health News (November 5th) independently calls it 'the $50 billion fund'. It's also consistent with C09 and C10.

claims.claim: Alaska's six program initiatives are Healthy Beginnings, Healthy Communities, Health Care Access, Strengthen Workforce, Spark Technology and Pay for Value.
claims.verbatim: Healthy Beginnings, supporting maternal and child health; Healthy Communities, focused on prevention and community well-being; Health Care Access, expanding care closer to home;
claims.notes: The sentence continues 'Strengthen Workforce, building and retaining Alaskan's health care workforce; Spark Technology, advancing digital and technology solutions; and Pay for Value, shifting toward payment models that reward quality and outcomes.' The funding update calls the tech initiative 'Spark Technology & Innovation'.

claims.claim: Norton Sound Health Corporation's Year 1 project will use cellular-enabled remote monitoring and daily check-ins to track high-risk chronic patients in Nome and 15 village clinics.
claims.verbatim: will use cellular-enabled remote monitoring and daily health check-ins to track high-risk patients with complex chronic conditions in Nome and 15 village clinics
claims.notes: The project is titled 'Direct Patient Monitoring for High-Risk Patients' and is listed under Spark Technology and Innovation. The CMS October 22nd release describes it without naming the grantee. The release doesn't call it AI, so don't describe it as AI.

claims.claim: Tanana Chiefs Conference's Year 1 Healthy Beginnings project will link clinics, health aides, doulas and telehealth into one maternal-infant care network across 32 communities.
claims.verbatim: telehealth into one maternal-infant care network across 32 communities
claims.notes: The CMS October 22nd release corroborates it, without the name, as a telehealth network in Interior Alaska across 32 communities.

claims.claim: Maniilaq Association's Year 1 award places portable X-ray units in Northwest Arctic village clinics.
claims.verbatim: Maniilaq Association ("Portable X-Ray Units for Rural Arctic Village Clinics") will place portable X-ray units in Northwest Arctic village clinics
claims.notes: The PDF prints curly quotes around the title, normalized to straight here. Health aides work with hospital providers by telehealth to decide faster whether an evacuation is needed.

claims.claim: Health Commissioner Heidi Hedberg said "This funding gives us the tools to help turn that vision into reality."
claims.verbatim: This funding gives us the tools to help turn that vision into reality.
claims.notes: The quote is verbatim on page 3, attributed to 'Alaska Department of Health Commissioner Heidi Hedberg'. It doesn't appear in the CMS October 22nd release. 'That vision' refers to her preceding sentence about a system that 'better serves every Alaskan, no matter where they live.'

claims.claim: The department plans to publish a dashboard of the full investment portfolio by the end of the calendar year.
claims.value: by the end of the calendar year
claims.verbatim: plans to publish a dashboard that allows Alaskans to explore the full portfolio of investments by the end of the calendar year.
claims.notes: This is a plan, not a delivered product, so say 'plans to'. As of the November 9th HTML fetch, the DOH page showed no dashboard.

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 2 fall funding cycle opened September 30th, with applications due October 28th.
claims.verbatim: The Year 2 fall funding cycle opened September 30, and applications are due Wednesday, October 28, at 11:59 pm.
claims.notes: The DOH HTML page corroborates it: the fall cycle 'opens on September 30, 2026' and closes October 28th at 11:59pm Alaska time. The deadline has passed as of the run date.

claims.claim: The state expects to notify Year 2 applicants as early as December, with Year 2 subawards beginning in early 2027.
claims.verbatim: DOH anticipates notifying applicants of outcomes as early as December 2026, with Year 2 subawards beginning in early 2027.
claims.notes: This is a projection, so use 'expects' or 'anticipates'.

claims.claim: A second Year 2 funding cycle is expected to open in spring 2027.
claims.verbatim: A second Year 2 funding cycle is anticipated to open in spring 2027.
claims.notes: This is a projection, so use 'expected to'.

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 1 project awards were announced in eight weekly rounds, the first on August 7th covering $4.5 million and 19 projects.
claims.verbatim: Week 1 | Aug 7 $4.5M Project Awards 19 Projects
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. WebFetch returned binary, and the fact-checker read the saved PDF directly. The verbatim is the text layer of a slide graphic. All eight rounds (dollars / projects) are Aug 7 $4.5M/19, Aug 14 $31.8M/37, Aug 21 $130M/104, Aug 28 $15.2M/23, Sept 4 $25.4M/32, Sept 18 $30.2M/27, Sept 25 $6.9M/7 and Oct 9 $4.8M/5. Dollars sum to $248.8M, which reconciles to $249M after rounding, and projects sum to 254. The amounts are projected as of October 9th (C45).

claims.claim: The largest weekly round, announced the week of August 21st, covered $130 million across 104 projects.
claims.verbatim: Week 3 | Aug 21 $130M Project Awards 104 Projects
claims.notes: Background. That's about 52 percent of Year 1 dollars in one week (derived). The CMS August 25th release ($160M for 142 projects, C49) appears to cover the first three weeks cumulatively ($4.5M + $31.8M + $130M = $166.3M, 160 projects). That reconciliation doesn't fully hold, so don't tie the two together on a slide. Preliminary per C45.

claims.claim: The final Year 1 round, on October 9th, covered $4.8 million across 5 projects.
claims.verbatim: $4.8M Project Awards 5 Projects Week 8 | Oct 9
claims.notes: Background. In the PDF text layer, the Week 8 label follows the figures. Preliminary per C45.

claims.claim: Alaska's Year 1 program is meant to reach each of Alaska's 30 boroughs and census areas.
claims.verbatim: strengthen the long-term sustainability of Alaska's rural health system across each of Alaska’s 30 boroughs and census areas.
claims.notes: The page prints mixed apostrophes, as kept here. This is a design intent ('designed to improve'), not proof that every borough received an award, so phrase it as 'designed to reach'. The same page shows a cumulative total of $249M and 254 projects.

claims.claim: The state cautions that its Year 1 amounts reflect projected awards as of October 9th and that minor adjustments may occur.
claims.verbatim: The data presented reflects projected award amounts as of October 9, and minor adjustments to award amounts may occur as the process is completed.
claims.notes: This caveat governs C41 to C47 and every workbook claim (C48 onward). The deck should carry a 'preliminary' or 'projected' qualifier on per-initiative and per-project dollar figures.

claims.claim: Health Care Access drew the largest share of Year 1 funding, $98.9 million or 40 percent.
claims.verbatim: Expanding access to behavioral health, pharmacy, dental, specialty, and primary care services $98.9M
claims.notes: Page 2 table, with 40% from the pie chart. The six initiative totals are Health Care Access $98.9M (40%), Spark Technology & Innovation $43.2M (17%), Pay for Value $32.2M (13%), Strengthen Workforce $30.1M (12%), Healthy Beginnings $22.7M (9%) and Healthy Communities $21.8M (9%). They sum to $248.9M and 100%. Projected as of October 9th.

claims.claim: Spark Technology and Innovation, the initiative for health technology, telehealth, electronic records and digital infrastructure, received $43.2 million or 17 percent of Year 1 funding.
claims.verbatim: Modernizing health technology, telehealth, electronic records, and digital infrastructure $43.2M
claims.notes: MINOR DISCREPANCY. The showrunner's workbook total for this initiative is $43,281,282 (C61), which rounds to $43.3M, not $43.2M. It's probably truncation or a post-October 9th adjustment. Use one figure consistently, either '$43.2 million' from the state's chart or 'about $43 million', and don't place both on a slide. Second largest of the six initiatives. Pay for Value $32.2M (13%), Strengthen Workforce $30.1M (12%), Healthy Beginnings $22.7M (9%) and Healthy Communities $21.8M (9%) appear on the same page.

claims.claim: The state's Notice of Intent to Award workbook lists 254 Year 1 awards totaling $248,976,547.51 in preliminary amounts.
claims.verbatim: Award Amount (Preliminary)
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook (column 'Award Amount (Preliminary)', summed over all 254 rows). The fact-checker couldn't fetch the xlsx. The DOH HTML page confirms that a Year 1 awards spreadsheet is linked there. date_of_source uses the October 9th final-notice date, and the workbook's own file date isn't independently checked. Consistent with 'just under $249 million' (C26). Don't call the amounts final. Seven AI-labeled awards are listed below (C49, C52 to C57), summing to $5,435,462.75, about 2.2 percent of the total (derived). The fact-checker can't confirm that list covers every AI-related row, so any AI total on a slide should read 'at least'.

claims.claim: In August, CMS highlighted more than $3.1 million in Alaska funding for a statewide AI imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals.
claims.verbatim: Over $3.1 million to establish a statewide AI imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (August 25th). The release is headlined 'Trump Administration Announces $160 Million to Bring Cutting-Edge Technology,...' and announces $160M for 142 Alaska projects (fetch summary). The grantee is the Alaska Stroke Coalition (C50), with a workbook amount of $3,156,626, which is consistent with 'over $3.1 million'. This primary source independently corroborates the largest AI award.

claims.claim: The Alaska Stroke Coalition's $3,156,626 award funds a statewide AI imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals for stroke and other emergencies.
claims.verbatim: a statewide AI imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals that pairs broad multi-pathology triage with advanced stroke imaging
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-042, titled 'Statewide Deployment of Clinical AI Decision Support Network Across Alaska Hospitals'. The summary also says 'stroke, hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, aortic and spinal injury' and 'Utilizing two complementary, cloud-based platforms that run on existing PACS without new imaging hardware'. The amount is preliminary. Its 21 hospitals and over $3.1M are corroborated by the CMS August 25th release (C49). It's the largest AI-labeled award in the set provided.

claims.claim: The AI imaging platforms in the Alaska Stroke Coalition project run on hospitals' existing PACS systems without new imaging hardware.
claims.verbatim: Utilizing two complementary, cloud-based platforms that run on existing PACS without new imaging hardware
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-042. This is the applicant's own description of its plan.

claims.claim: MapHabit Inc received $1,241,085.55 for AI-powered visual maps for people with developmental disabilities, brain injury and Alzheimer's-related dementias, starting in Mat-Su and the Kenai Peninsula.
claims.verbatim: AI-powered visual maps for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, traumatic brain injury, and Alzheimer's-related dementias
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-200. The initial focus is the Mat-Su and Kenai Peninsula Boroughs. The amount is preliminary. MapHabit is an out-of-state vendor, which the deck may note only if it confirms that elsewhere.

claims.claim: Maniilaq Association received $430,000 for behavioral health AI clinical documentation, citing documentation burden as a driver of therapist turnover.
claims.verbatim: the documentation burden has been cited as a driver of therapist turnover.
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-194, titled 'Behavioral Health AI Clinical Documentation'. The turnover point is the applicant's framing, so attribute it with 'Maniilaq says'. The amount is preliminary. This is separate from Maniilaq's portable X-ray award (C35).

claims.claim: Mat-Su Regional Medical Center received $250,000 for AI-assisted EEG using a single-use headband a nurse can apply, potentially avoiding transfers to Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: a single-use, eight-lead headband, which a nurse can rapidly apply
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-202, titled 'AI-Assisted EEG'. The device determines 'if a patient is experiencing status epilepticus', 'potentially avoiding the need for a costly, time-sensitive transfer away from the Mat-Su into Anchorage.' The transfer benefit is the applicant's projection, so keep 'potentially'. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: Ptarmigan Pediatrics received $190,556 for a patient portal and Nuance DAX ambient AI voice technology to automate clinical charting.
claims.verbatim: Nuance DAX ambient AI voice technology to automate clinical charting
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-272 (Ptarmigan Pediatrics LLC). The portal serves '16,500 patients'. The application's 'reducing charting time by 50%' is a vendor or applicant projection, not a measured result. Don't put 50% on a slide unless it's framed as 'the practice expects' or 'aims to'. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: The Statewide Independent Living Council received $141,702.70 for an AI assistive technology needs assessment tool.
claims.verbatim: AI Assistive Technology Needs Assessment Tool
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-319. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: Kodiak Community Health Center received $25,492.50 for an AI-supported clinical documentation platform, the smallest AI-labeled award in the set reviewed.
claims.verbatim: AI-supported clinical documentation platform
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-187. 'Smallest' holds only within the seven AI awards the showrunner supplied, so phrase it as 'as small as' rather than 'the smallest' unless the showrunner confirms a full scan. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: Bartlett Regional Hospital received $231,669 to convert its electronic health records, saying its clinics' separate systems can't access emerging AI tools.
claims.verbatim: cannot access emerging AI tools and functions
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-064, titled 'Bartlett EHR Conversion'. This is an EHR purchase, not an AI purchase, so don't count it in any AI total. The verbatim keeps the source's 'cannot', as the house rule allows for quoted text. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: PeaceHealth Ketchikan Medical Center's preliminary award of $6,967,728.14 funds the first robotic-assisted minimally invasive surgeries in Southern Southeast Alaska.
claims.verbatim: the first robotic assisted minimally invasive surgeries
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-254. DISCREPANCY: the CMS August 25th release (primary) says '$6.5 million to introduce the first robotic assisted minimally invasive surgeries to Southern Southeast Alaska.' The workbook's preliminary figure is about $468K higher. Use either 'about $7 million in the state's preliminary award list' or 'CMS cited $6.5 million in August', and don't present both as the same number. Robotic surgery isn't AI, so don't count it in an AI total.

claims.claim: CMS cited $6.5 million in August for the first robotic-assisted minimally invasive surgeries in Southern Southeast Alaska.
claims.verbatim: $6.5 million to introduce the first robotic assisted minimally invasive surgeries to Southern Southeast Alaska.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. See C59 for the conflicting workbook figure.

claims.claim: CMS cited $4.75 million in August to expand Alaska's health information exchange.
claims.verbatim: $4.75 million to strengthen Alaska’s statewide health data infrastructure by expanding health information exchange.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The page prints a curly apostrophe. No grantee was named or verified.

claims.claim: CMS cited a quarter million dollars in August to develop the framework for a drone-based medication delivery system connecting villages across 94,000 square miles.
claims.verbatim: A quarter million dollars to develop the regulatory, technical, and community engagement framework
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The fetch summary says the framework is for drone-based pharmaceutical delivery connecting villages across 94,000 square miles. It matches the Tanana Chiefs planning award (C63), with the same $250,000 and 94,000 square miles.

claims.claim: Tanana Chiefs Conference received a $250,000 planning award for drone medication delivery linking its Fairbanks hub to 42 Interior villages across 94,000 square miles, with UAF's ACUASI as partner.
claims.verbatim: connecting TCC's Fairbanks hub to 42 Interior Alaska villages across 94,000 square miles
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-PL-026, a planning year. The summary continues 'where medication delivery delays of 5 to 14 days are common during winter', but the workbook prints that range with an en dash, so quote it only with the dash normalized or paraphrase it. The 5 to 14 day figure is the applicant's claim, so attribute it. The CMS August 25th release corroborates the $250,000 and 94,000 square miles (C62). It's a planning award, so nothing is flying yet.

claims.claim: Ryan Air received $4,171,115 to bring autonomous cargo drones and electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft to the Bethel and Dillingham regions.
claims.verbatim: autonomous cargo drones and electric vertical take-off and landing (EVTOL) aircraft
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, row BP1-IA-284. It describes planned deployment, not operating service, so use 'plans to' or 'to bring'. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: The workbook lists 47 Spark Technology and Innovation awards totaling $43,281,282.
claims.verbatim: Spark Technology and Innovation
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, initiative column aggregation. $43,281,282 rounds to $43.3M, against the state chart's $43.2M (C47). See that note, and pick one figure. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: Health Care Access accounts for 102 of the 254 Year 1 awards in the workbook.
claims.verbatim: Health Care Access
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, initiative column count. About 40 percent of awards by count, matching its 40 percent share of dollars (C46), which is derived.

claims.claim: Of the 254 Year 1 awards, 26 are planning awards totaling $5,464,210 and 228 are implementation awards.
claims.verbatim: Planning
claims.notes: Parsed by the showrunner from the state workbook, award type column. Row ids prefixed BP1-PL are planning and BP1-IA are implementation. 26 + 228 = 254 checks out. The amount is preliminary.

claims.claim: The seven Year 1 awards whose titles or summaries say they buy or build an AI tool total $5,435,462.75, about $5.4 million, about 2.2 percent or roughly two cents of each dollar of the $248,976,547.51 the workbook lists.
claims.notes: Sum computed by the showrunner from the seven rows in C50 and C52 to C57. 2.18 percent of C48, printed as about 2.2 percent and as about two cents of every dollar. Bartlett's EHR conversion (C58) mentions AI only as something its old systems can't reach and is not counted. A project that uses AI without saying so in its title or summary would be missed, so the deck says at least.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

claims.claim: The Alaska Stroke Coalition award's service area in the workbook is Statewide, and its summary names none of the 21 hospitals.
claims.verbatim: BP1-IA-042 ... Statewide ... a statewide AI imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals
claims.notes: Service Area column reads exactly Statewide. The summary gives the count 21 and no hospital names.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

claims.claim: MapHabit's AI award and the Statewide Independent Living Council's AI award are both filed with a Statewide service area.
claims.verbatim: BP1-IA-200 ... Statewide ; BP1-IA-319 ... Statewide
claims.notes: MapHabit's summary adds an initial focus on the Matanuska-Susitna and Kenai Peninsula Boroughs (C52).
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

claims.claim: The three AI awards filed as Statewide total $4,539,414.25, about $4.5 million of the AI total.
claims.notes: Sum of C50, C52 and C56 by the showrunner. 83.5 percent of C68.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

claims.claim: The other four AI awards name their service areas, Matanuska-Susitna Borough for Mat-Su Regional and Ptarmigan Pediatrics, Kodiak Island Borough for Kodiak Community Health Center, and North Slope Borough and Northwest Arctic Borough for Maniilaq.
claims.verbatim: BP1-IA-202 Matanuska-Susitna Borough; BP1-IA-272 Matanuska-Susitna Borough; BP1-IA-187 Kodiak Island Borough; BP1-IA-194 North Slope Borough;Northwest Arctic Borough
claims.notes: Service Area column, verbatim.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

claims.claim: Every one of Alaska's 30 boroughs and census areas is named in at least one Year 1 award's service area in the workbook, and 68 awards are filed as Statewide.
claims.verbatim: Service Area column counts, 68 rows read Statewide
claims.notes: Counted by the showrunner; the Copper River Census Area appears under two spellings.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

claims.claim: Year 2 workload funding for Alaska works out to $172,653,149, Alaska's $272,653,149 award less the $100 million baseline every state gets.
claims.notes: Derived from C02 and C14 by the showrunner; CMS does not print this figure.
claims.source_outlet: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, with the baseline from the CMS Year 2 fact sheet

claims.claim: The part of Alaska's Year 1 award not in the workbook's project subawards comes to $23,198,308.21, about $23.2 million, which the state says supports administration, evaluation and oversight.
claims.verbatim: 272,174,855.72 minus 248,976,547.51; The remaining award balance supports administration, evaluation and oversight of the RHTP program.
claims.notes: Derived by the showrunner from C30 less C48; the purpose is the state's own sentence (C24).
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Year 1 Notice of Intent to Award workbook

stories_surviving: Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program, with a $272.7 million Year 2 award second only to Texas and a roughly $249 million Year 1 portfolio across 254 projects, including where AI appears in it

killed.claim: Rural areas are expected to lose about $137 billion, according to KFF (Stateline, Nada Hassanein, via Alaska Beacon, November 9th).
killed.why: Alaska Beacon, stateline.org and newsfromthestates.com all returned HTTP 403, so the page wasn't fetched. It's single-sourced secondary reporting of a KFF projection, and the KFF Health News article I did fetch didn't surface it. Unverified.

killed.claim: Stateline reported that Texas received the largest grant, almost $282 million, followed by Alaska, Montana, California and Oklahoma.
killed.why: The Stateline page returned 403 on every mirror tried. The ranking itself is verified from the primary CMS table (C03 to C07), so use those claims and don't attribute it to Stateline.

killed.claim: Half of the annual $10 billion is split equally among states (as a verbatim 'half' statement).
killed.why: The fetch confirmed the $100 million per state per year baseline verbatim (C14) but returned no verbatim string for 'half'. The halving is folded into C14 and C15 as arithmetic, $100M x 50 = $5B, rather than as a quoted claim.

killed.claim: The Alaska DOH RHTP web page shows the breakdown of Year 1 funding across initiatives, names the six initiatives, and gives the $249 million and 254 projects totals.
killed.why: None of that appears in the fetched HTML of https://health.alaska.gov/en/education/rural-health-transformation-program/, which only links the update PDF and spreadsheet. The figures are verified from the PDFs instead (C26, C27, C32, C46, C47). The HTML page is cited only for the $272,174,855.72 Year 1 award and the Year 2 cycle dates.

killed.claim: The CMS October 22nd release names Norton Sound, Tanana Chiefs and Maniilaq, quotes Heidi Hedberg and gives Alaska's $272 million Year 1 award.
killed.why: The fetched CMS October 22nd release does none of that: it names no grantees, has no Hedberg quote and gives no $272M figure. Those facts are verified from the Alaska DOH release PDF instead (C28, C33 to C36).

killed.claim: RUNNER-UP, the RCA approved an Enstar and MEA gas exchange (Petroleum News November 1st, Alaska Public Media November 6th).
killed.why: No article URLs were supplied, and an alaskapublic.org site search surfaced no matching story. Petroleum News wasn't reachable without a URL, so I fetched nothing. Every runner-up claim is unverified and the fallback story doesn't survive. The lead story stands on its own.
